title: "Output Intent Missing" or "No ICC Profile": How to Fix Your Print PDF | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix "output intent is missing" or "no ICC profile" in your PDF
description: Your print PDF says it's PDF/X-1a but has no output intent or ICC profile, so it fails the check. What that means in plain English and how to fix it.
lead: This one sounds technical, but it's just a missing label inside your file that tells the printer what kind of printing it was made for.
error: PDF/X-1a output intent is missing or has no embedded ICC profile
errorNote: Paraphrased from preflight checks (Acrobat and printer systems word it differently).
why:
A PDF/X-1a file must carry an output intent: a note saying which printing conditions the colors were prepared for, usually with an ICC profile (a small color description) built in. That's how the printer knows how to read your CMYK colors.

Files often lose it when they're re-saved, merged or "optimized" in a different program, or when a tool labels a file PDF/X-1a without doing the full job. Checks then fail even though the pages look fine.
manual: Go back to your original design file (InDesign, Affinity, Illustrator).
Export again using the built-in "PDF/X-1a:2001" preset. Don't re-save it in another app afterwards.
No InDesign? In Acrobat Pro, open Print Production → Preflight and run "Convert to PDF/X-1a", choosing a CMYK profile such as US Web Coated (SWOP) v2.
Run Preflight again to confirm "PDF/X-1a compliant".
Re-upload it to your printer and wait for the file review again. If it fails, you start over.

cta.text: SparkPrep exports a full PDF/X-1a with the output intent and color profile built in, every time, with no Acrobat Pro needed.

faq.q: What is an output intent in a PDF?
faq.a: A note inside a print PDF that says which printing conditions its colors were prepared for, usually with an ICC color profile embedded.

faq.q: Which ICC profile should I use?
faq.a: Use the one your printer recommends. US Web Coated (SWOP) v2 is a common choice for US book printing.
